newsitem.title: CHINA: China okays six shippers for direct Taiwan route.
newsitem.headline: China okays six shippers for direct Taiwan route.

text.p: China has given approval to six domestic firms to begin direct shipping services with Taiwan, the China Business Times said on Thursday.
The Ministry of Communications has cleared six ships owned by the six Chinese shipping firms for direct sailings, it quoted officials in eastern Fujian province, which faces Taiwan, as saying.

The six shipping firms are the Fujian branch of China Ocean Shipping (Group), Fujian Provincial Shipping Co, Fujian Xiamen Shipping Co, Fujian Foreign Trade Centre Shipping Co, the China National Foreign Trade Corp's Fujian Shipping Co and Fujian Mawei Shipping Co, it said.
China has previously reported that five shipping firms had won approval to conduct direct sailings, but did not give the number of ships involved or other details.

Fujian province has been investing heavily in construction of sea ports, airports, roads, power projects and telecommunications facilities in recent years to prepare for direct shipping links, the newspaper said.
To guarantee the safety of the shipping routes, the province has removed blocks from sea beacons and set up new lighthouses on the Chinese side, it said.
Fujian would also open coastal radio stations to meet the vessels' communications needs, it added.
Eight shipping firms from Taiwan have filed applications to Fujian authorities to engage in direct shipping, it said.
They include Taiwan's Yang Ming Marine Transport Corp, Chinese Maritime Transport, Uniglory Marine Corp and Wan Hai lines, it said.
Taiwan has banned direct trade with rival China since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 although it has allowed commercial ties through other territories, usually Hong Kong.
But it has come under increasing pressure from its own businessmen as well as from Beijing to permit direct shipping and air links.
The two sides have reached agreement on direct crossings between Taiwan's southern port of Kaohsiung and China's port of Xiamen with inaugural sailings expected as early as this week.
Taipei says it is limiting the new service to connections with Kaohsiung for transshipment to destinations not on Taiwan.
